entries.text: Your "power walk" is so gentle, a flock of pigeons refused to move out of your way.
You walk so slow, Google Maps keeps asking if you're stuck in traffic.
You track your steps so loosely, chewing gum counts as a half-mile.
Your jogging pace is so casual, you can hold a full conversation with a statue.
Your cool-down walk is somehow faster than your actual workout.
Your pace is so leisurely, a box turtle just gave you the "on your left" warning.
You walk so slow, your shadow is getting bored and walking ahead of you.
You're so inflexible, your Downward Dog looks like a Sad Plank.
Your Child's Pose is so comfortable, you've used it to take three separate naps today.
You stretch so rarely, your joints sound like bubble wrap popping under a boot.
Your Tree Pose is so unstable, a gentle breeze could knock you into next week.
You spend so much time in Savasana, the yoga instructor almost called a paramedic.
Your Warrior Pose looks more like a Worried Pose.
You're so stiff, your attempt at touching your toes is just a polite nod to your knees.
Your yoga mat is so thick and plush, it's legally classified as a mattress.
You hold a stretch for so short, a camera shutter moves slower than you do.
Your balance is so bad, you managed to fall over while sitting cross-legged.
You treat the yoga studio like a day spa that just happens to have floor mats.
Your weights are so light, they actually float if you drop them.
You lift those 1-pound pink dumbbells like you're carrying live nuclear waste.
Your resistance band is so thin, it looks like a piece of mint-flavored dental floss.
You do bicep curls with soup cans and still look around for a spotter.
Your dumbbells are so small, they could easily fit inside a Kinder Joy egg.
You lift weights so light, a stiff breeze could steal your entire workout.
Your workout weights are lighter than the phone you're scrolling on between sets.
You struggled with that 2-pound weight so hard, the shadow of it pinned you to the floor.
Your resistance training is so low-impact, the resistance is entirely psychological.
You lift weights so light, you could genuinely wear them as statement earrings.
Your dumbbells are so tiny, they look like lost Monopoly pieces.
Your idea of "cardio" is walking around the grocery store looking for free samples.
You do jumping jacks so low, your sneakers never actually leave the ground.
You do chair exercises so comfortably, the chair is doing 99% of the manual labor.
Your idea of a circuit workout is walking from the couch to the fridge and back.
Your high knees look like you're just trying not to step on a stray Lego.
You do jumping jacks so quietly, a sleeping baby wouldn't even stir.
Your workout video is so retro and gentle, Richard Simmons would tell you to tone it down.
Your low-impact routine has less impact than a feather landing on a silk pillow.
Your fitness tracker is so bored, it just vibrated to suggest you go take a nap.
You spend more time picking out a playlist than you do actually moving your body.
Your water bottle is significantly bigger than the amount of effort you're putting in.
You check your heart rate so often, you're basically just taking your own pulse for fun.
Your sweatband is completely bone-dry, but your workout is somehow already over.
You burned more calories driving to the park than you did walking around it.
Your fitness tracker genuinely thought you were asleep during your entire workout.
You spend so much time resting between stretches, your muscles are actively getting colder.
Your activewear is so pristine, it still smells exactly like the department store rack.
You call it a workout, but your Fitbit just logged it as "aggressive sitting."
